financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone) basis. EPS 0.25 = 71,766,724 / 285,341,744 confirmed. operating_profit derived the same way as the Group row (87,175,107). capex same as Group (60,417,073) -- the Company's larger net investing outflow (104,673,098 vs Group's 56,742,918) is mainly a 47,919,582 investment in a subsidiary, which is not included in capex.

Software/SaaS company (HR/HCM software, 'Lexi' AI platform) -- no extraction issues, verified via EPS 0.18 = 51,029,050 / 285,341,744 shares in issue. operating_profit = gross profit + other income - administrative expenses - selling & marketing expenses - other operating expenses (65,762,699), a derived subtotal since the filing goes straight from those line items to PBT (after finance cost/income) without a separate 'operating profit' subtotal of its own. capex = acquisition of PPE (1,869,050) + intangible assets (48,176,126) + capitalised contract costs (10,371,897) = 60,417,073, all real capitalised outflows for this business. long_term_borrowings = 0: the non-current liabilities line for interest-bearing borrowings is nil at this date (the entire non-current liabilities balance, 166,014,529, is the retirement benefit obligation).

interim_updates.note_text: hSenid Business Solutions (hBS) posted Group revenue of Rs.602.8mn for Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 28% YoY, driven by subscription revenue as recurring revenue grows as a share of the total. The Group swung from a Rs.35.7mn loss to a Rs.51.0mn profit (+243% YoY). Per the CEO's own commentary, foreign exchange gains contributed to profitability, but core operating performance also improved genuinely: EBITDA excluding forex gains reached Rs.81.4mn at a 14% margin, up from just 0.3% in the same quarter last year. Gross profit rose 48% YoY to Rs.321.8mn (53% margin), and PBT swung from a Rs.40.0mn loss to a Rs.66.1mn profit (+265% YoY). Management attributes the turnaround to sustained revenue growth combined with operating leverage as the business scales, and cited continued investment in the 'Lexi' AI platform (multi-agent orchestration capabilities released this quarter) as part of its Human Capital Operating System roadmap.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for HBS -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. EPS basic pct_change is not shown (prior period was a loss, crossing zero makes a percentage change not meaningful) -- direction is shown as 'improved' instead.
interim_updates.takeaway: A genuine, largely organic turnaround -- the CEO's own disclosure separates the FX-driven boost from core operating improvement, and the core number (EBITDA ex-forex margin 0.3% to 14%) is the more important one: gross margin expansion (46% to 53%) and operating leverage as recurring/subscription revenue scales, not a one-off currency gain, is what's driving this.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.602.8mn, up 28% YoY, driven by subscription revenue and a growing recurring-revenue share
Group swung from a Rs.35.7mn loss to a Rs.51.0mn profit (+243% YoY); PBT swung from a Rs.40.0mn loss to a Rs.66.1mn profit (+265% YoY)

Core operating performance (management's own EBITDA excluding forex gains) improved from a 0.3% margin to 14% (Rs.81.4mn) -- the CEO explicitly separates this from the FX-gain contribution to reported profit
Gross profit up 48% YoY to Rs.321.8mn, gross margin 53% (vs 46% a year earlier)
Released multi-agent orchestration capabilities on the 'Lexi' AI platform this quarter, part of the company's Human Capital Operating System roadmap
Net cash used in operating activities (Group: -Rs.5.9mn) despite the strong P&L, driven by a Rs.132.2mn increase in trade and other receivables -- a working-capital, not profitability, item
key_drivers: Revenue growth (28% YoY) combined with operating leverage -- administrative expenses grew only 4% YoY while revenue grew 28%, expanding margins as the business scales, per management's own framing

The CEO explicitly quantifies and separates the FX contribution: reported PAT growth (+243%) partly reflects foreign exchange gains, but core EBITDA margin (ex-forex) still improved dramatically (0.3% to 14%), indicating genuine operating improvement beneath the currency effect

Working capital absorbed cash despite strong reported profit -- trade and other receivables grew Rs.132.2mn (Group) during the quarter, turning operating cash flow negative (-Rs.5.9mn) even as PAT was positive (Rs.51.0mn) -- worth watching whether this reverses as a collections-timing issue or persists

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
